From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: AWS private offer request + co-sell interest (GridWorks)

Soojin — thx for the heads-up. Pricing guidance: 15% standard discount for first-year marketplace private offers up to $150k ARR without C-level signoff. 20% requires SRM or VP approval unless we trade for a longer term or a committed growth clause. Options to hit 20%:
- Move to a 24-month term with 10% upfront and 10% on signed 12-month renewal (structure a multi-year commitment), or
- Keep 12-month term, cap discount at 15% and include a 12-month MBO for expansion credits that effectively increase net ARR if they hit usage targets.

Co-sell: we can register the opportunity in AWS PRM once the PO or purchase order intent is in place. Co-sell registration typically takes 2-5 business days to get formal acknowledgement; won't block the private offer creation but AWS tends to prefer registration before spending credits.

If you want me to escalate to SRM for a one-off 20% we need to provide: projected ARR, exec sponsor, justification for discount (strategic co-sell value or referenceability). If GridWorks is only $120k and not strategic, pushing for 20% will be tough.

Recommend: offer 15% on 12 months now, include a 12-month expansion credit tied to usage (documented in the buyer-approver checklist), and promise to register for co-sell immediately. If buyer insists on 20%, I'll route to SRM but need their exec sponsor name.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, GTM Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FW: AWS private offer request + co-sell interest (GridWorks)

Team — legal/contract notes:
- Marketplace private offers still bind the buyer to AWS terms for the transaction, but Redwood should provide a short addendum or SOW that covers service levels and any professional services not delivered via the SKU. Keep the addendum minimal (1–2 pages) and non-conflicting with AWS marketplace terms.
- If procurement requires a PO-based invoicing flow, confirm the billing entity (GridWorks legal name) and whether they need a Redwood-issued invoice post-transaction (we normally rely on AWS for billing; exceptions are handled via an additional commercial agreement).
- For co-sell registration, ensure we capture: customer AWS account ID and the AWS seller lead. That will speed PRM registration.

I can draft a one-page addendum. If you want to offer 20% and need legal approval for an exception, give me the proposed commercial justification and I will review.

—Vanessa
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Emma / Theo — thanks for the quick turn. Per internal guidance below, here's the path we can execute this week to meet your Nov 15 close target:

1) Pricing & term: We will issue an AWS Marketplace private offer for a 12-month term at 15% off list (RDW list SKU: rdw.analytics.annual). To bridge to 20%, we can add an expansion credit schedule (see attached pricing worksheet) that tiers additional credits at usage milestones — effectively approximating your target economics if usage expands.

2) Co-sell: We will register the opportunity in APN/PRM once you provide your AWS account ID and executive sponsor. Registration will be submitted same day and typically returns approval within 2–5 business days. This will allow AWS to provide co-sell support and list the opportunity in their pipeline.

3) Procurement flow: Because billing will go through AWS, procurement will receive AWS-generated invoices. If your procurement team requires a Redwood invoice, we can prepare one post-transaction under a supplementary commercial agreement; please confirm. Also attach: buyer-approver-checklist.pdf — please complete with approver names + emails and return so we can populate the private-offer buyer approver list.

4) Next steps:
- Emma: confirm AWS account ID and the final list of approvers by Mon 9 Nov EOD.
- Theo: if you want me to pursue SRM escalation for deeper discount, please provide the exec sponsor name and strategic rationale; otherwise we'll proceed at 15% with the expansion credit construct.

Attaching: pricing worksheet (xlsx), buyer approver checklist (pdf), brief AWS private-offer instructions (txt).

I'll prepare the addendum template and send it for your review; none of the marketplace terms change — it's purely a short SOW for services.

Thanks — looking forward to the details.

Cheers,
